page.definition_block: Wind energy engineers design wind-farm layouts and turbine parameters, using aerodynamic and structural simulations to evaluate loads and grid integration while balancing generation efficiency, equipment life, and site conditions.

rows.label: Work Environment
rows.value: Mostly a mix of office and on-site work, varying by role.

rows.label: Entry Requirement
rows.value: A relevant bachelor's degree is the mainstream entry route

rows.label: Core Output
rows.value: Professional outputs and decisions related to Wind Energy Engineers.

rows.label: Skill Requirements
rows.value: Strong Wind Energy Engineers expertise + tool proficiency.

rows.label: Working Relationships
rows.value: Reporting upward, coordinating across teams, communicating externally.

rows.label: Scope of Responsibility
rows.value: Professional judgment and final sign-off rest with people.

responsibilities_block: Assess wind resources and perform micrositing and layout design.
Simulate blade aerodynamics, loads, and tower structures.
Design electrical connections and grid-integration plans.
Develop operations and maintenance strategies and assess service life.
Use SCADA data to diagnose performance deviations.
Write technical specifications and support bidding and acceptance.
page.work_context_block: In the morning, run wind-resource models and adjust turbine spacing. Around midday, use finite-element analysis to examine tower deformation under extreme wind. Later, write the electrical-interconnection plan, then use SCADA to investigate an underperforming turbine. In the evening, revise specifications with curves and three-dimensional turbine-layout drawings side by side on the screen.
